territorial_scope.description: Applies in Ohio; exemptions are granted by agreement with named taxpayers and their projects.

evidence.quote: A taxpayer that proposes a capital improvement project for an eligible computer data center in this state may apply to the tax credit authority

summary.short: Ohio statute letting the Tax Credit Authority exempt, by agreement, computer data center equipment at eligible data centers from state sales and use taxes, subject to investment and payroll tests. In force from September 30, 2025.
summary.long: Section 122.175 lets the Ohio Tax Credit Authority, under agreements with taxpayers proposing data center projects, fully or partly exempt from state sales and use tax the computer data center equipment used at eligible facilities. Eligibility requires project payments of at least one hundred million dollars over three to six consecutive calendar years and annual compensation of at least 1.5 million dollars subject to withholding. The Tax Commissioner and Director of Development review applications for economic impact. Approval requires increased payroll, economic soundness, ability to maintain operations, and that the exemption be a major factor in the investment decision. Agreements fix the exemption percentage (up to 100 percent), term, annual reporting, a limit on relocating employment without notice, and a waiver of limitations periods. Taxpayers use a direct payment permit and file returns. For noncompliance the authority may reduce the exemption or terminate the agreement and recover prior taxes. The Director adopts rules, reports annually by 1 August, and the statute is effective September 30, 2025.

"Computer data center business" means, as may be further determined by the tax credit authority, a business that provides electronic information services as defined in division (Y)(1)(c) of section 5739.01 of the Revised Code

enforcement.triggered_by: A taxpayer subject to an exemption agreement fails to meet or comply with any condition or requirement set forth in the agreement.
enforcement.max_penalty_text: The authority may reduce the percentage of the exemption or the term during which the exemption applies for the noncompliant taxpayer's equipment; no maximum reduction is stated.
enforcement.penalty_formula: Reduction of the exemption percentage or of the exemption term, as amended by the authority; the reduction may take effect in the current calendar year.

evidence.quote: the tax credit authority may amend the agreement to reduce the percentage of the exemption or term

enforcement.triggered_by: The director of development determines that a taxpayer's exempted computer data center no longer complies with the requirement in division (E)(3) (remaining an eligible computer data center and maintaining operations), after notice and an opportunity for the taxpayer to explain the noncompliance.
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Termination of the agreement and payment to the state of all or a portion of the taxes that would have been owed on the exempt equipment in previous years, as determined by the authority; no fixed maximum is stated.
enforcement.penalty_formula: Amount set by the authority from taxes that would have been owed on the exempt equipment in previous years, considering market conditions, whether the taxpayer keeps other Ohio operations, and each taxpayer's share of responsibility; the tax commissioner assesses that amount, and the assessment must be made within one year after the authority certifies the amount, with the normal assessment time limits not applying.
enforcement.cure_period: None stated; before termination each taxpayer is given an opportunity to explain the noncompliance.
